To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the chemical and biological properties of condensed tannins isolated from purple prairie clove (Dalea pupurea Vent.) were affected by the conservation method.

(a) conservation method did not affect total CT concentration, but ensiling increased the proportion of fiber-bound CT, (b) hay-making and ensiling decreased the protein-precipitability of CT, (c) ensiling decreased the proportion of EGC in the terminal unit of CT and increased the proportion of PC, and (d) hay-making retained more biologically-active CT than ensiling.
ensiling decreased extractable CT and protein-precipation capacity of CT, whereas hay-making only increased protein-bound CT.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of conservation method on CT in PPC.
the effect of foraging and preservation methods on CT concentration and structure in PPC, which is an emerging legume for livestock and wildlife production.
the characterization of condensed tannins in forages conserved as hay or silage and the effects on their bioactivity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
conservation method affects both the structural and biological activity of PPC CT.
the conservation method affected both chemical and biological activity of the CT in PPC.
the conservation method of PPC affected CT concentration, chemical composition, mDP, protein-precipation capacity and biological activity of PPC CT.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ensiling of PPC decreased the protein-precipitate capacity of CT by decreasing the extractable and increasing the fiber-bound CT.
ensiling decreased extractable CT and the protein-precipitatin capacity of CT, but hay-making only increased protein-bound CT.
ensiling decreased extractability of CT by increasing fiber-bound CT, and that hay-making only increased protein-bound CT, but not fiber-bound CT.
The main takeaway from our work is that
conservation method can affect the biological activity of plant CT, but the effect is likely to depend on the plant species and the CT structural composition.
the chemical composition of PPC CT was altered by conservation method, and the effect of conservation method on CT chemical composition was not consistent.
CT from PPC are more bioavailable in hay than in silage.
